questions.q: The Pandya Kingdom was first mentioned by Megasthenes, who said that their kingdom was famous for pearls. Their capital was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madurai.

Key Points

• Madurai was the capital of the ancient Pandya Kingdom, known for its flourishing trade and cultural heritage.

• The city is famous for the Meenakshi Amman Temple, a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River.

• It has been a major settlement for two millennia and is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

• Madurai has a rich historical background and has been mentioned in ancient texts and inscriptions, highlighting its significance during the Pandya rule.

Additional Information

• Pandya Kingdom

• The Pandya Kingdom was one of the three ancient Tamil kingdoms, the other two being the Chola and the Chera kingdoms.

• The Pandyas were known for their contributions to Tamil literature, art, and architecture.

• Their rule is dated back to several centuries BCE, and they were contemporary to other South Indian dynasties like the Cholas and the Cheras.

• The Pandyas were great patrons of the Tamil language and literature, which flourished under their rule.

• Megasthenes

• Megasthenes was a Greek historian and diplomat who served as an ambassador to the court of Chandragupta Maurya in India.

• His work "Indica" provides an account of the Indian subcontinent during the Maurya Empire, including descriptions of the people, culture, and geography.

• Megasthenes' writings are considered valuable historical sources for understanding ancient India.

• Meenakshi Amman Temple

• The Meenakshi Amman Temple is dedicated to Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort, Sundareshwar, a form of Shiva.

• The temple complex is a significant symbol of South Indian architecture, featuring tall gopurams (gateway towers) adorned with intricate carvings.

• The temple is a major pilgrimage site and attracts millions of visitors and devotees annually.

questions.q: Harivarasanam award is given in the field of music by which of the following state governments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kerala.

Key Points

• The Harivarasanam Award is given annually by the Kerala state government to honor individuals for their contributions to the field of music.

• The award is named after the famous song "Harivarasanam," which is dedicated to the deity Ayyappa and is sung at the Sabarimala Temple in Kerala.

• This award recognizes the achievements and contributions of musicians who have made significant impact in the realm of devotional and classical music.

• The award includes a cash prize, citation, and a plaque, which are presented to the recipient during a ceremony organized by the Kerala government.

Additional Information

• Harivarasanam

• Harivarasanam is a Sanskrit devotional song dedicated to Lord Ayyappa.

• It is also known as the "Lullaby Song" because it is sung just before the temple closes for the night.

• The song describes the glory and virtues of Lord Ayyappa, and is an integral part of the rituals at the Sabarimala Temple.

• The song was composed by Kambangudi Kulathur Srinivasa Iyer and was popularized by the renowned singer K.J. Yesudas.

• Sabarimala Temple

• Sabarimala Temple is one of the most famous pilgrimage centers in India, located in the Pathanamthitta district of Kerala.

• The temple is dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, and it attracts millions of devotees every year, especially during the Mandala season (mid-November to mid-January).

• Sabarimala is known for its unique customs, including the strict 41-day vratham (fasting and abstinence) that devotees must observe before visiting the temple.

• The temple is situated amidst dense forests and mountains, symbolizing the spiritual journey and the ultimate union with the divine.

• Devotional Music

• Devotional music plays a significant role in the cultural and spiritual life of India.

• It encompasses a wide range of genres including bhajans, kirtans, qawwalis, and more, each associated with different religious and spiritual traditions.

• Devotional music is often performed in temples, religious ceremonies, and spiritual gatherings, serving as a medium for expressing devotion and reverence towards the divine.

• Many renowned musicians and composers have contributed to the rich tradition of devotional music in India, making it an integral part of the country's cultural heritage.

questions.q: Easter festival is celebrated by which community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Christian.

Key Points

• Easter is one of the most significant festivals in Christianity, marking the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.

• This festival is celebrated on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the vernal equinox.

• Easter is the culmination of the Passion of Jesus, preceded by Lent, a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance.

• The Easter festival also includes traditions such as Easter eggs and the Easter Bunny, which symbolize new life and rebirth.

Additional Information

• Easter:

• Easter is a festival and holiday commemorating the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, described in the New Testament as having occurred on the third day of his burial after his crucifixion by the Romans at Calvary c. 30 AD.

• It is the culmination of the Passion of Jesus, preceded by Lent (or Great Lent), a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance.

• Most Christians refer to the week before Easter as "Holy Week"—it contains the days of the Easter Triduum, including Maundy Thursday (commemorating the Maundy and Last Supper), as well as Good Friday (commemorating the crucifixion and death of Jesus).

• In Western Christianity, Easter is always celebrated on the Sunday following the first full moon that occurs on or after the spring equinox.

• Christianity:

• Christianity is an Abrahamic monotheistic religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth. It is the world's largest religion, with about 2.4 billion followers.

• Its adherents, known as Christians, believe that Jesus is the Christ, whose coming as the Messiah was prophesied in the Hebrew Bible, called the Old Testament in Christianity, and chronicled in the New Testament.

• Christian theology is summarized in creeds such as the Apostles' Creed and the Nicene Creed, which state that Jesus suffered, died, was buried, descended into hell, and rose from the dead, and ascended into heaven, from where he will return.

• Christianity is divided into three main branches: Catholicism, Orthodoxy, and Protestantism.

questions.q: Which of the following Sikh reform movements was started in 1873 in Amritsar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Singh Sabha Movement.

Key Points

• The Singh Sabha Movement was a Sikh reform movement started in 1873 in Amritsar.

• It aimed at reforming the Sikh community by promoting education and a return to the teachings of the Sikh Gurus.

• The movement was a reaction to the proselytizing activities of Christian missionaries and the Arya Samaj, which were seen as a threat to Sikhism.

• It played a significant role in the revival of Sikh institutions, literature, and the Punjabi language.

Additional Information

• Babbar Akali Movement:

• This was a militant movement in the 1920s aimed at freeing India from British rule.

• The Babbar Akali Dal was formed by a group of Sikh farmers in Punjab.

• They were against British policies and sought to restore Sikh sovereignty.

• It was named "Babbar" (lion) to denote the fierce nature of the movement.

• Akali Movement:

• The Akali Movement (also known as the Gurudwara Reform Movement) was a campaign in the early 20th century to reform the management of Sikh gurudwaras.

• It aimed at removing corrupt mahants (custodians) appointed by the British government.

• The movement led to the formation of the Shiromani Gurudwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC).

• The SGPC now oversees the management of gurudwaras in Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh.

• Gurudwara Movement:

• This movement is synonymous with the Akali Movement mentioned above.

• It focused on freeing Sikh places of worship from the control of corrupt mahants.

• The movement gained momentum in the 1920s and led to significant reforms in the management of Sikh religious institutions.

• It was a major milestone in the history of the Sikhs and their religious autonomy.

questions.q: 'Bhagirathi' and 'Alaknanda' rivers confluence at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Devprayag.

Key Points

• Devprayag is a town and a nagar panchayat (municipality) in Tehri Garhwal district in the state of Uttarakhand, India.

• It is one of the Panch Prayag (five confluences) of Alaknanda River, where Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers meet and take the name Ganges or Ganga.

• Devprayag is situated at an altitude of 830 meters (2,723 feet) above sea level.

• The town is a significant pilgrimage site for Hindus, and the confluence point is considered sacred.

Additional Information

• Bhagirathi River:

• The Bhagirathi River is one of the two headstreams of the Ganges, the other being the Alaknanda.

• It originates from the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand and flows for approximately 205 kilometers before meeting the Alaknanda at Devprayag.

• The Bhagirathi River is named after King Bhagiratha who, according to Hindu mythology, brought the river Ganga to Earth.

• Alaknanda River:

• The Alaknanda River is another major tributary of the Ganges.

• It originates at the confluence of the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers in Uttarakhand.

• The river flows for about 190 kilometers before joining the Bhagirathi at Devprayag.

• Alaknanda is considered a sacred river and is closely associated with Hindu mythology and pilgrimage sites.

• Devprayag:

• Devprayag is the first of the Panch Prayag, the five sacred confluences in the Garhwal Himalayas.

• The town is famous for its temples and the sacred confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers.

• It is a starting point for the Char Dham pilgrimage, which includes Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath.

• Devprayag is also known for the Raghunathji Temple, dedicated to Lord Rama.

questions.q: Identify a spiral-shaped bacteria.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Spirillum.

Key Points

• Spirillum is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria characterized by their spiral shape.

• They are typically found in stagnant freshwater environments and are known for their unique helical structure.

• Spirillum bacteria are motile, meaning they can move, using flagella located at both ends of the cell.

• These bacteria are often used in microbiological studies to understand bacterial motility and structure.

Additional Information

• Bacillus

• Bacillus is a genus of rod-shaped, Gram-positive bacteria.

• These bacteria are commonly found in soil and water and are known for their ability to form endospores.

• Examples include Bacillus anthracis, which causes anthrax, and Bacillus subtilis, a model organism for laboratory studies.

• Coccus

• Coccus refers to any bacterium that has a spherical, ovoid, or generally round shape.

• They can exist as single cells or in clusters, chains, and other formations.

• Examples include Staphylococcus (clusters) and Streptococcus (chains).

• Vibrio

• Vibrio is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria, possessing a curved-rod (comma) shape.

• They are typically aquatic and can cause diseases such as cholera (caused by Vibrio cholerae).

• Vibrio bacteria are facultative anaerobes, meaning they can survive with or without oxygen.

Key Points

• The Government of India Act, 1935, introduced the concept of 'provincial autonomy' in British India.

• This Act marked the end of the system of dyarchy introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919.

• Under provincial autonomy, provinces were given more authority and independence in their internal administration.

• Indian ministers, chosen by provincial legislatures, were given authority in provincial governments, reducing the British governors' power.

Additional Information

• Government of India Act, 1919

• Also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.

• Introduced the concept of dyarchy in the provinces, splitting the provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.

• Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor and his Executive Council, while transferred subjects were administered by Indian ministers responsible to the legislative council.

• Charter Act of 1813

• It ended the East India Company's commercial monopoly in India, opening trade to private British merchants.

• Asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Indian territories held by the Company.

• Provided for the promotion of education in India.

• India Council Act, 1909

• Also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.

• Introduced separate electorates for Muslims, a measure designed to provide representation to minorities.

• Increased the size of the legislative councils at both the central and provincial levels.

questions.q: Which committee recommended Constitutional recognition for the local government bodies in 1989?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is PK Thungon Committee.

Key Points

• The PK Thungon Committee was formed in 1988 to review the working of the Panchayati Raj institutions.

• The committee recommended Constitutional recognition for the local government bodies.

• It suggested the establishment of three-tier Panchayati Raj system in the states.

• The recommendations led to the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which were enacted in 1992 and came into effect in 1993.

Additional Information

• Panchayati Raj System

• The Panchayati Raj system is a form of local self-government in rural India.

• It was introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992.

• The system consists of three levels: the Gram Panchayat (village level), the Panchayat Samiti (block level), and the Zila Parishad (district level).

• This system aims to decentralize the administration and promote local governance.

• 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act

• It was enacted in 1992 and came into effect on 24 April 1993.

• This amendment provided a constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions.

• It introduced Article 243 to 243O in Part IX of the Constitution.

• The Act mandates the establishment of Panchayats at the village, intermediate, and district levels in all states and Union territories.

• It also provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women.

• 74th Constitutional Amendment Act

• It was enacted in 1992 and came into effect on 1 June 1993.

• This amendment provided a constitutional status to the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).

• It introduced Article 243P to 243ZG in Part IXA of the Constitution.

• The Act mandates the establishment of Municipalities in urban areas.

• It also provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT related to reticulate venation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maize.

Key Points

• Maize exhibits parallel venation, which is typical of monocotyledonous plants.

• In parallel venation, veins run parallel to each other, which is different from reticulate venation where veins form a network.

• Examples of plants with parallel venation include grasses, lilies, and maize.

• Reticulate venation is commonly found in dicotyledonous plants like China rose and Tulsi.

Additional Information

• Venation

• Venation refers to the arrangement of veins in the leaf blade.

• It is important for the identification of plant species and helps in the distribution of nutrients and water throughout the leaf.

• Reticulate Venation

• Reticulate venation is characterized by a net-like pattern of veins.

• It is commonly found in dicots such as China rose, Tulsi, and Coriander.

• In this type of venation, the main vein (midrib) branches into secondary veins which further branch into tertiary veins forming a network.

• Parallel Venation

• Parallel venation is characterized by veins running parallel to each other.

• It is typical of monocots such as Maize, wheat, and other grasses.

• In this type of venation, veins do not form a network but run parallel from the base to the tip of the leaf.

• Examples of Plants

• China Rose (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis) - Exhibits reticulate venation.

• Tulsi (Ocimum tenuiflorum) - Exhibits reticulate venation.

• Maize (Zea mays) - Exhibits parallel venation.

• Coriander (Coriandrum sativum) - Exhibits reticulate venation.

questions.q: In which of the following Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka is the Kalinga war mentioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is XIII.

Key Points

• The Kalinga War is mentioned in the Major Rock Edict XIII of Ashoka.

• This edict provides details about the war, its aftermath, and Ashoka's remorse over the bloodshed and suffering caused.

• Edict XIII also highlights Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism and his efforts towards spreading Dhamma (moral law).

• The edict emphasizes Ashoka's change of heart and his dedication towards non-violence and the welfare of his subjects.

Additional Information

• Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka

• The Major Rock Edicts are a set of 14 inscriptions that were issued by Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Dynasty around 250 BCE.

• These edicts are found across various parts of the Indian subcontinent, including modern-day India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Afghanistan.

• The edicts focus on ethical and moral teachings, emphasizing non-violence, tolerance, and respect for all forms of life.

• Ashoka's edicts also promote social welfare, justice, and the importance of following the Dhamma.

• Kalinga War

• The Kalinga War was fought between the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka and the state of Kalinga (present-day Odisha) around 261 BCE.

• The war is renowned for its massive scale and the significant loss of life and suffering it caused.

• Ashoka's experience in the aftermath of the war led to his deep remorse and a transformative shift in his beliefs.

• The Kalinga War played a pivotal role in Ashoka's adoption of Buddhism and his subsequent efforts to promote peace and non-violence.

• Ashoka the Great

• Ashoka was the third emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, ruling from approximately 268 to 232 BCE.

• He is widely remembered for his role in spreading Buddhism and his emphasis on moral governance.

• Ashoka's reign marked a period of significant cultural and religious transformation in ancient India.

• His legacy is celebrated for his contributions to the promotion of non-violence, social welfare, and the spread of Buddhist teachings.

questions.q: Who among the following is NOT a member of the National Human Rights Commission?

• Human rights include the rights to life, liberty, equality, and dignity of individuals guaranteed by the Indian Constitution and enforceable by courts in India.

• The NHRC investigates complaints of human rights violations, conducts inquiries, and makes recommendations to the government.

questions.q: Which of the following is an inosilicate amphibole mineral used in highway construction and as railroad ballast?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hornblende.

Key Points

• Hornblende is an inosilicate amphibole mineral found in many types of igneous and metamorphic rocks.

• It is commonly used in highway construction and as railroad ballast due to its hardness and durability.

• Hornblende can be identified by its dark color, usually green to black, and its elongate, prismatic crystals.

• It is composed of double chain SiO₄ tetrahedra linked at the vertices and generally contains calcium, iron, and magnesium.

Additional Information

• Inosilicates:

• Inosilicates, also known as chain silicates, are a group of silicate minerals that form chains of SiO4 tetrahedra linked together by sharing oxygen atoms.

• There are two types of chain structures: single chains and double chains.

• Single chain inosilicates include minerals like pyroxenes, while double chain inosilicates include amphiboles like hornblende.

• Amphibole Minerals:

• Amphiboles are a group of inosilicate minerals that form prism or needle-like crystals.

• They are typically hydrous (contain water in their structure) and can include various elements such as iron, magnesium, calcium, and aluminum.

• Amphiboles are important rock-forming minerals found in both igneous and metamorphic rocks.

• Railroad Ballast:

• Railroad ballast is the gravel or coarse stone used to form the bed of a railroad track.

• It provides stability, drainage, and support for the weight of the trains.

• Materials used for ballast include crushed stone, gravel, or other durable materials, such as hornblende.

• Highway Construction:

• In highway construction, durable materials like hornblende are used for various purposes including base layers, subbase layers, and as aggregate in asphalt or concrete.

• These materials provide strength, stability, and longevity to the constructed highways.

questions.q: Identify a monoatomic molecule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Helium.

Key Points

• Helium is a noble gas and is represented by the symbol He.

• It is the second lightest and second most abundant element in the observable universe.

• Helium is a monoatomic gas, meaning it exists as single atoms rather than molecules.

• It is chemically inert and does not easily form compounds with other elements.

Additional Information

• Monoatomic Molecule

• A monoatomic molecule consists of a single atom, unlike diatomic or polyatomic molecules which consist of two or more atoms.

• Examples of monoatomic molecules include noble gases like Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), and Xenon (Xe).

• These elements exist as individual atoms because their outer electron shells are complete, making them highly stable and unreactive.

• Carbon Monoxide (CO)

• Carbon monoxide is a diatomic molecule consisting of one carbon atom and one oxygen atom.

• It is a colorless, odorless, and highly toxic gas.

• CO is produced by the incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels.

• Oxygen (O₂)

• Oxygen is a diatomic molecule consisting of two oxygen atoms.

• It is essential for respiration in most living organisms.

• Oxygen makes up about 21% of the Earth's atmosphere.

• Chlorine (Cl₂)

• Chlorine is a diatomic molecule consisting of two chlorine atoms.

• It is a greenish-yellow gas with a strong, pungent odor.

• Chlorine is used in water purification, disinfectants, and the production of many consumer products.

questions.q: Which of the following chemical reactions takes place when quick lime reacts with water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq).

Key Points

• Quick lime is chemically known as calcium oxide (CaO).

• When quick lime reacts with water, it forms calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2), also known as slaked lime.

• This reaction is exothermic, meaning it releases heat.

• The chemical equation for this reaction is: CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq).

Additional Information

• Quick Lime (Calcium Oxide)

• Quick lime, or calcium oxide (CaO), is a white, caustic, alkaline substance.

• It is produced by heating limestone (calcium carbonate, CaCO3) to a high temperature, a process known as calcination.

• CaO is widely used in industrial processes such as steelmaking, chemical production, and wastewater treatment.

• Calcium Hydroxide

• Calcium hydroxide, also known as slaked lime, is a compound with the chemical formula Ca(OH)2.

• It is a white powdery substance that forms when calcium oxide reacts with water.

• Ca(OH)2 is used in the construction industry to make mortar and plaster, in the food industry for processing water and as a food additive, and in various chemical processes.

• Exothermic Reactions

• An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that releases energy in the form of heat or light.

• In the reaction of calcium oxide with water, the release of heat is significant enough to make the mixture hot and sometimes boiling.

• Exothermic reactions are used in various applications, including heat packs, combustion engines, and industrial manufacturing processes.

questions.q: If the 9-digit number 5x79856y6 is divisible by 36, then what is the negative value of (2x+y)​ for the largest possible value of y, given x and y are natural numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Divisibility by 36 requires checking divisibility by both its co-prime factors, 4 and 9.

For divisibility by 4, the last two digits 'y6' must be a multiple of 4 ⇒ largest single digit y = 9.

For divisibility by 9, the sum of digits (5+x+7+9+8+5+6+9+6 = 55+x) must be a multiple of 9 ⇒ x = 8.

The negative value of √(2x + y) = −√(2 × 8 + 9) = −√25 = −5.

∴ The correct answer is −5.

Alternate Method

Given:

A 9-digit number 5x79856y6 is divisible by 36.

x and y are natural numbers.

Formula Used:

A number is divisible by 36 if it is divisible by both 4 and 9.

Divisibility by 4: The number formed by the last two digits must be divisible by 4.

Divisibility by 9: The sum of all digits must be divisible by 9.

Calculations:

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 4, the last two digits 'y6' must be divisible by 4.

⇒ Since y is a natural number, the possible single-digit values for y are 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9.

⇒ We are asked to find the answer for the largest possible value of y, so we take y = 9.

⇒ Substituting y = 9 gives the number 5x7985696.

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 9, the sum of its digits must be a multiple of 9.

⇒ Sum of digits = 5 + x + 7 + 9 + 8 + 5 + 6 + 9 + 6

⇒ Sum of digits = 55 + x

⇒ The closest multiple of 9 greater than 55 is 63.

⇒ 55 + x = 63

⇒ x = 63 − 55 = 8

⇒ We need the negative value of √(2x + y):

⇒ √(2x + y) = √(2 × 8 + 9)

⇒ √(16 + 9) = √25 = ±5

⇒ The negative value is −5.

∴ The correct answer is −5.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Composite Divisibility

questions.q: Anna and Ben each have a collection of marbles. If Anna gives one marble to Ben, they will both have an equal number of marbles. Conversely, if Ben gives one marble to Anna, she will end up with three times the number of marbles that Ben has. What is the total number of marbles they both have?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

From the first condition, Anna has 2 more marbles than Ben. Thus, Total = 2 × Ben + 2, which must be an even number.

Eliminate the odd options (11 and 9); verify the even options starting with 8.

If Total = 8, then Ben = 3 and Anna = 5.

Checking the second condition: If Ben gives 1 to Anna, Anna gets 6 and Ben is left with 2.

Since 6 is exactly 3 × 2, this satisfies all the given conditions perfectly.

∴ The correct answer is 8 marbles.

Alternate Method

Given:

Let the initial number of marbles with Anna be A and with Ben be B.

Final Verified Distribution

Anna:

(5 Marbles)

Ben:

(3 Marbles)

•
Total = 5 + 3 = 8 Marbles

Calculations:

Case 1: If Anna gives one marble to Ben, they have an equal number.

⇒ A − 1 = B + 1

⇒ A = B + 2 (Equation 1)

Case 2: If Ben gives one marble to Anna, she has three times as many as Ben.

⇒ A + 1 = 3 × (B − 1)

⇒ A + 1 = 3B − 3 (Equation 2)

Substitute Equation 1 into Equation 2:

⇒ (B + 2) + 1 = 3B − 3

⇒ B + 3 = 3B − 3

⇒ 2B = 6

⇒ B = 3

Now find the number of marbles Anna has using Equation 1:

⇒ A = 3 + 2 = 5

Find the total number of marbles for both:

⇒ Total = A + B

⇒ Total = 5 + 3 = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8 marbles.

Additional Information

Linear Equations in Two Variables

A mathematical system of two linear equations models relationships between two unknowns. Such simultaneous equations can be efficiently solved using the substitution or elimination method.

Translating Word Problems

Common transaction phrases like 'gives 1 to' mean subtracting from the giver and adding to the receiver simultaneously, maintaining the same total item count overall.

Option Testing Strategy

For aptitude problems embedded with multiple linked conditions, testing the given multiple-choice options backward is often faster than setting up and solving long algebraic formulas.

questions.q: If A : B = 6 : 8 and B : C = 7 : 12, then A : B : C is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simplify A : B = 6 : 8 ⇒ 3 : 4.

Given B : C = 7 : 12.

Using the shifted-neighbor method for combining ratios:

A : B : C = (3 × 7) : (4 × 7) : (4 × 12)

A : B : C = 21 : 28 : 48

∴ The correct answer is 21 : 28 : 48.

Alternate Method

Given:

A : B = 6 : 8

B : C = 7 : 12

Calculations:

⇒ First, simplify the ratio A : B to its lowest terms.

⇒ A : B = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4

⇒ To combine the ratios, make the common term (B) equal in both expressions.

⇒ The LCM of 4 and 7 is 28.

⇒ Multiply the A : B ratio by 7 ⇒ A : B = (3 × 7) : (4 × 7) = 21 : 28

⇒ Multiply the B : C ratio by 4 ⇒ B : C = (7 × 4) : (12 × 4) = 28 : 48

⇒ Now that B is equal in both ratios (28), we can combine them directly.

⇒ A : B : C = 21 : 28 : 48



∴ The correct answer is 21 : 28 : 48.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied term-wise, the resulting ratio is called a compound ratio. For a:b and c:d, the compound ratio is ac:bd.

Duplicate Ratio

The ratio of the squares of two numbers is called their duplicate ratio. The duplicate ratio of a:b is a²:b².

Invertendo Rule

If a : b = c : d, then by the invertendo property, taking the reciprocal of both sides gives b : a = d : c.

questions.q: A man can row a distance of 6 km in 1 hour in still water. He can row the same distance in 45 minutes with the current. Find the total time taken by him to row a distance of 16 km with the current and to return to the starting point.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Downstream speed = Distance ÷ Time = 6 ÷ (45/60) = 8 km/h.

Stream speed = Downstream speed − Still water speed = 8 − 6 = 2 km/h.

Upstream speed = Still water speed − Stream speed = 6 − 2 = 4 km/h.

Total Time = Downstream Time + Upstream Time = (16 ÷ 8) + (16 ÷ 4)

Total Time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of the man in still water (Vb) = 6 km/h

Distance covered downstream = 6 km

Time taken downstream = 45 minutes = 45 ÷ 60 = 3/4 hours

Distance for final trip = 16 km each way

Formulas Used:

Downstream Speed (Vd) = Vb + Speed of stream (Vₛ)

Upstream Speed (Vᵤ) = Vb − Vₛ

Time = Distance ÷ Speed



Calculations:

⇒ Downstream Speed (Vd) = Distance ÷ Time = 6 ÷ (3/4) = 8 km/h

⇒ We know Vd = Vb + Vₛ

⇒ 8 = 6 + Vₛ ⇒ Vₛ = 2 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (Vᵤ) = Vb − Vₛ = 6 − 2 = 4 km/h

⇒ Time taken to row 16 km downstream = 16 ÷ 8 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken to row 16 km upstream = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 hours

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours

∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Additional Information

Downstream Speed

When a boat moves in the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the sum of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current. Formula: D = Vb + Vₛ

Upstream Speed

When a boat moves against the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current. Formula: U = Vb − Vₛ

Speed of Boat and Stream from D and U

Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 | Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2

questions.q: If 3a + 2b = 27 and 27a³ + 8b³ = 1458, then find 2ab.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the derived algebraic identity: x³ + y³ = (x + y)[(x + y)² − 3xy]

Let x = 3a and y = 2b, which means xy = (3a)(2b) = 6ab.

⇒ 1458 = 27 × [27² − 3 × (6ab)]

⇒ 54 = 729 − 18ab

⇒ 18ab = 675 ⇒ ab = 37.5

∴ The correct answer is 75.

Alternate Method

Given:

3a + 2b = 27

27a³ + 8b³ = 1458

Formula Used:

(x + y)³ = x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y)

Calculation:

Let x = 3a and y = 2b, so we need to find 2ab.

⇒ (3a + 2b)³ = (3a)³ + (2b)³ + 3 × (3a) × (2b) × (3a + 2b)

⇒ 27³ = 27a³ + 8b³ + 18ab(3a + 2b)

Substitute the given values into the expanded formula:

⇒ 19683 = 1458 + 18ab × 27

⇒ 19683 − 1458 = 486ab

⇒ 18225 = 486ab

⇒ ab = 18225 ÷ 486

⇒ ab = 37.5

Now, multiply by 2 to find the required value of 2ab:

⇒ 2ab = 2 × 37.5 = 75

∴ The correct answer is 75.

Additional Information

Algebraic Cube Identities

• (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

• (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)

Sum of Cubes

• a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

Difference of Cubes

• a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

questions.q: Simplify the given expression 3y−2x4x2+9y2−12xy​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Recognize that the numerator is a perfect square trinomial.

4x² + 9y² − 12xy = (3y − 2x)²

The given fraction reduces to: (3y − 2x)² ÷ (3y − 2x)

Canceling the common term gives: 3y − 2x

∴ The correct answer is 3y − 2x.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: (4x² + 9y² − 12xy) ÷ (3y − 2x)

Formula Used:

(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

Calculations:

⇒ Rewrite the numerator in the form of a² − 2ab + b²

⇒ Numerator = (2x)² + (3y)² − 2 × (2x) × (3y)

⇒ This simplifies to (2x − 3y)²

⇒ Since squaring a negative gives a positive, (2x − 3y)² is identical to (3y − 2x)²

⇒ Substitute this back into the fraction: (3y − 2x)² ÷ (3y − 2x)

⇒ Dividing by the common factor (3y − 2x) yields: 3y − 2x

∴ The correct answer is 3y − 2x.

Additional Information

Perfect Square Trinomial

An algebraic expression obtained by squaring a binomial. The key formulas are: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Difference of Two Squares

A squared number subtracted from another squared number. The standard identity is: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

Sum and Difference of Cubes

For sum and difference of cubed terms, the formulas are: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

The product of two sine terms can be converted to a difference of cosine terms directly using standard trigonometric identities.

The trigonometric expression is sin A × sin B

Expansion of cosine formulas:

questions.q: An investor, invested ₹2,00,000 in shares. The shares rose by 18% on the first day, fell by 15% on the second day, and then fell by 3% on the third day. What is the net percentage increase or decrease in the value of the investor's shares? (Rounded up to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use successive percentage formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) / 100

Effective change for +18% and −15%: 18 − 15 − (18 × 15) / 100 = 3 − 2.7 = 0.3%

Effective change for +0.3% and −3%: 0.3 − 3 − (0.3 × 3) / 100 = −2.7 − 0.009 = −2.709%

The negative sign represents a decrease. Rounding to one decimal place gives a 2.7% decrease.

∴ The correct answer is decrease by 2.7%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial investment = ₹2,00,000

Successive changes: +18%, −15%, −3%



Formula Used:

Net Value = Initial Value × (100 ± R₁)/100 × (100 ± R₂)/100 × (100 ± R₃)/100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial value of shares be 100 (since the final answer is a percentage, the base of ₹2,00,000 is not needed).

⇒ Value after Day 1 = 100 × 118/100 = 118

⇒ Value after Day 2 = 118 × 85/100 = 100.3

⇒ Value after Day 3 = 100.3 × 97/100 = 97.291

⇒ Net Percentage Change = 97.291 − 100 = −2.709%

⇒ Since the result is negative, it indicates a decrease of approximately 2.7%.

∴ The correct answer is decrease by 2.7%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is calculated using the formula: a + b + (a × b) / 100. Use a negative sign for any decrease.

Independence of Base Value

When solving for a net percentage change, the actual initial amount is completely redundant. Assuming a base of 100 always simplifies the calculation.

Multiplying Factor Method

An increase of x% gives a multiplying factor of (1 + x/100), while a decrease of x% gives (1 − x/100). The overall multiplying factor is the product of all individual factors.

questions.q: Aman borrows a sum of ₹192208 at the rate of 15% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹20196 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Aman clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total amount to clear the dues = (Total amount of original loan for 2 years) − (Amount of the repaid part for the remaining period).

Total amount for original loan for 2 years at 15% SI = ₹192208 + (₹192208 × 15% × 2) = ₹192208 + ₹57662.4 = ₹249870.4

Amount of the repaid part for the remaining 1 year = ₹20196 + (₹20196 × 15% × 1) = ₹20196 + ₹3029.4 = ₹23225.4

Remaining dues at the end of 2nd year = ₹249870.4 − ₹23225.4 = ₹226645.

∴ The correct answer is ₹226645.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹192208

Rate of Interest (R) = 15% per annum

Principal repaid at the end of 1st year = ₹20196

Formula Used:

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = P + SI



Calculations:

⇒ Interest for the 1st year = (192208 × 15 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹28831.2

⇒ After repaying ₹20196 towards principal, the remaining principal for the 2nd year = 192208 − 20196 = ₹172012

⇒ Interest for the 2nd year on the new principal = (172012 × 15 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹25801.8

⇒ Total pending dues at the end of 2nd year = Remaining Principal + Interest for 1st year + Interest for 2nd year

⇒ Total dues = 172012 + 28831.2 + 25801.8 = ₹226645

∴ The correct answer is ₹226645.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

The interest is calculated strictly on the original principal for the given period. The interest itself does not earn interest. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Partial Repayment in SI

When a partial payment is made towards the principal amount, the simple interest for the subsequent periods is calculated on the newly reduced principal balance.

Total Amount (Dues)

The total sum of money to be cleared at the end of a loan tenure includes both the final remaining principal and all unpaid accrued interest. Formula: Amount = P + SI.

questions.q: A seller sold 19 cookies for ₹95 instead of 20 cookies in one kg, cheating a customer. What is the gain (in ₹) if the seller bought the cookies for ₹76?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cost price of 1 cookie = ₹76 ÷ 20 = ₹3.8

Since the seller gives 19 cookies, the actual cost incurred = 19 × ₹3.8 = ₹72.2

Selling price collected from the customer = ₹95

Gain = Selling Price − Cost Price = 95 − 72.2 = ₹22.8

∴ The correct answer is ₹22.8.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total cost price of 1 kg (20 cookies) = ₹76

Total selling price of the transaction = ₹95

Number of cookies actually given to the customer = 19



Formula Used:

Gain = Total Selling Price − Total Cost Price Incurred

Total Cost Price = Cost Price of 1 unit × Actual Quantity Given

Calculations:

⇒ Cost price of 1 cookie = 76 ÷ 20 = ₹3.8

⇒ Cost incurred by the seller for giving 19 cookies = 19 × 3.8 = ₹72.2

⇒ Selling price collected from the customer = ₹95

⇒ Gain = SP − CP incurred

⇒ Gain = 95 − 72.2 = ₹22.8

∴ The correct answer is ₹22.8.

Additional Information

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer cheats by altering the true quantity or weight, the effective Cost Price must be calculated based only on the items actually handed over to the customer, not on the promised or standard quantity.

Profit and Loss Basics

Gain occurs when the total Selling Price (SP) is greater than the total Cost Price (CP) incurred. It is calculated as Gain = SP − CP. The Profit Percentage is always calculated on the base of CP: (Gain ÷ CP) × 100.

Successive Markup and Quantity Cheat

If a seller marks up the price and simultaneously cheats in quantity, the overall profit combines both effects. You can calculate it directly by taking the ratio of the total money received (SP) to the total money spent (actual CP).

questions.q: Find the area (in cm²) of the sector, where the radius of the circle is 24 cm and length of the arc is 7 cm.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The area of a circular sector can be calculated directly if the arc length and radius are given.

Area of Sector = (Arc Length × Radius) ÷ 2

Area = (7 × 24) ÷ 2

Area = 168 ÷ 2 = 84

∴ The correct answer is 84 cm².

Given:

⇒ Radius of the circle (r) = 24 cm

⇒ Length of the arc (l) = 7 cm

Formula Used:

⇒ Area of a Sector = (θ ÷ 360) × π × r²

⇒ Arc Length (l) = (θ ÷ 360) × 2 × π × r

⇒ By substituting Arc Length in the Area formula: Area = (l × r) ÷ 2

Calculations:

⇒ Area = (7 × 24) ÷ 2

⇒ Area = 168 ÷ 2

⇒ Area = 84 cm²

∴ The correct answer is 84 cm².

Additional Information

Area of a Sector with Central Angle

When the central angle θ is given in degrees, the area is calculated using the formula: Area = (θ ÷ 360) × π × r².

Perimeter of a Sector

The perimeter includes the length of the arc and the two radii enclosing it. It is computed as: Perimeter = l + 2 × r.

Area of a Circle

The total area covered by a complete circle is evaluated using the formula: Area = π × r².

Arc Length Formula

The length of an arc spanning a central angle θ is given by: l = (θ ÷ 360) × 2 × π × r.

questions.q: If the selling price of an article is ₹1,792 after a 20% discount, then the marked price of the article is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Discount = 20% = 1/5

If Marked Price is 5 units, Selling Price will be 5 − 1 = 4 units.

⇒ 1 unit = 1792 ÷ 4 = ₹448

⇒ Marked Price (5 units) = 448 × 5 = ₹2,240

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,240.

Alternate Method

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,792

Discount = 20%



Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

Calculations:

⇒ MP = (1792 × 100) ÷ 80

⇒ MP = 179200 ÷ 80

⇒ MP = 17920 ÷ 8

⇒ MP = 2240

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,240.

Additional Information

Marked Price & Discount Base

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article, not the Cost Price (CP). The selling formula is: Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If an article is subject to two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount can be calculated using the formula: (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Markup Percentage

The percentage by which a seller increases the Marked Price over the original Cost Price is called the Markup Percentage. It is given by: MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100).

questions.q: What is the volume of a cone (in cubic units) with radius of 3 units and slant height 3√2 units?
options: 310π​
39π​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By the relation between slant height (l), radius (r), and height (h) of a cone: h = √(l² − r²).

h = √((3√2)² − 3²) = √(18 − 9) = √9 = 3 units.

Volume of a cone = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h.

Volume = (1 ÷ 3) × π × 3² × 3 = 9π.

∴ The correct answer is 9π cubic units.

Alternate Method



Given:

Radius of the cone (r) = 3 units

Slant height of the cone (l) = 3√2 units

Formula Used:

Volume of cone (V) = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h

Pythagorean relation for a cone: l² = r² + h²

Calculations:

⇒ First, find the height (h) of the cone.

⇒ l² = r² + h²

⇒ (3√2)² = 3² + h²

⇒ 18 = 9 + h²

⇒ h² = 18 − 9

⇒ h² = 9

⇒ h = √9 = 3 units

⇒ Now, substitute the calculated height into the volume formula:

⇒ V = (1 ÷ 3) × π × (3)² × 3

⇒ V = (1 ÷ 3) × π × 9 × 3

⇒ V = 9π cubic units

∴ The correct answer is 9π cubic units.

Additional Information

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a Cone

The area of only the curved side is calculated using the formula CSA = π × r × l, where r is the radius and l is the slant height.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cone

The total surface area includes the circular base along with the curved surface. It is given by TSA = π × r × (r + l).

Relationship with a Cylinder

A cylinder having the exact same base radius (r) and height (h) as a cone will always have exactly three times the volume of the cone. Cylinder Volume = π × r² × h.
